data.one_liner: A performant, Express.js-like web server and REST API framework for Dart.
data.what_it_does: Alfred is a web server and REST API framework inspired by Express.js. It features automatic type handling for responses, built-in body parsing, file uploads, routing with parameter validation, middleware support, and CORS handling.
use_when: You want to build a lightweight REST API or web server in Dart with familiar Express.js patterns.
You need automatic response serialization for JSON, plain text, and binary/files.
avoid_when: You are building a client-side Flutter application UI.
You require full integration with pre-built ecosystem servers like Shelf if your architecture strictly depends on it.
strengths: Express.js-like routing and syntax that is easy to learn.
Minimal dependencies and close adherence to Dart core libraries.
Built-in type handlers that automatically resolve responses based on return types.
weaknesses: Less extensive ecosystem compared to larger Node.js frameworks.
Not documented for advanced features beyond standard REST and routing use cases without custom type handlers.
